# rustinion_alert_rule (Resource)

Manages a Rustinion alert rule: an AND/OR combination of metric conditions, evaluated on a schedule with hysteresis. See web/src/alerting.rs in the main repo for full evaluation semantics.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `group_id` (String) ID of the group this alert rule belongs to.
- `name` (String)

### Optional

- `bool_op` (String) Combine conditions with "and" (every condition must breach) or "or" (any one does). Defaults to "and".
- `breaches_to_fire` (Number) Consecutive breaching evaluations before the rule fires. Defaults to 3.
- `clears_to_resolve` (Number) Consecutive healthy evaluations before a firing rule clears. Defaults to 2.
- `condition` (Block List) One metric condition. A rule with no conditions never breaches. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--condition))
- `enabled` (Boolean)
- `escalation_policy_id` (String) Escalation policy to notify when this rule fires, in the same group. Omit for none.
- `severity` (String)

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Server-assigned alert rule ID.

<a id="nestedblock--condition"></a>
### Nested Schema for `condition`

Required:

- `comparator` (String) For a threshold or forecast condition: gt, gte, lt, lte, or eq (eq is not valid for forecast). For an anomaly condition, only gt/lt/eq are valid (above/below/either direction from baseline). For a composite condition this attribute is required by the schema but not meaningful server-side — use "eq", matching the admin UI's own convention.
- `metric_type` (String) A builtin metric type (e.g. "cpu_avg_pct"), "custom:<name>", "slo_burn_rate:<uuid>", "rum:<app_id>:<vital>" (e.g. "rum:<uuid>:LCP"), "k8s_event_count:<reason>" (e.g. "k8s_event_count:OOMKilled"), "new_error_groups:<service_name>", "error_rate:<service_name>:<operation_name>", or (computed server-side, sent as any placeholder for a composite condition) "composite:<uuid>".
- `threshold` (Number) The threshold value, or (for an anomaly condition) the sensitivity in standard deviations from the baseline. For a composite condition this attribute is required by the schema but not meaningful server-side — use 0, matching the admin UI's own convention.

Optional:

- `aggregation` (String) How to combine this metric's values across every device in the group before comparing it to threshold: "avg" (default), "sum", "min", "max", or a percentile ("p50", "p90", "p95", "p99"). Only meaningful for a `custom:<name>` metric_type.
- `anomaly_method` (String) Required for an anomaly condition: "rolling_stddev" or "seasonal". Unused for a threshold or forecast condition.
- `baseline_window_minutes` (Number) Required for an anomaly condition: how far back its baseline is computed from, in minutes.
- `composite_expect_firing` (Boolean) Only valid for a composite condition: `true` (the server's own default when omitted) breaches when the referenced rule IS firing; `false` breaches when it is NOT firing. Deliberately not `Computed`/defaulted here (unlike most other attributes in this schema) — a computed default would mean Terraform always sends *some* value for it on every condition, including non-composite ones, which the server rejects outright (`composite_rule_id/composite_expect_firing are only valid for condition_kind = "composite"`); leaving it purely `Optional` means it's only ever sent when the config actually sets it.
- `composite_rule_id` (String) Required for a composite condition: the id of another `rustinion_alert_rule` in the same tenant (e.g. `rustinion_alert_rule.other.id`) whose current firing state this condition reads instead of a metric. Must not be this rule's own id, and must belong to this same tenant — both enforced server-side.
- `condition_kind` (String)
- `forecast_within_hours` (Number) Required for a forecast condition: how soon (in hours) the metric's current linear trend must be projected to cross `threshold` for this condition to breach. Datadog calls this shape a "Forecast Monitor" — alerts before a threshold is actually crossed, not just after.
- `mw_long_threshold` (Number) Required for a slo_burn_rate_multi_window condition: the LONG window's own burn-rate threshold (e.g. 6 for a 6h/6x pairing with a 1h/14.4x short window).
- `mw_long_window_minutes` (Number) Required for a slo_burn_rate_multi_window condition: the LONG window's own lookback, in minutes (e.g. 360 for 6h). Paired with window_minutes above, which is reused as the SHORT window's own lookback — fires only when BOTH windows independently breach their own threshold (threshold above is the short window's threshold; mw_long_threshold below is the long window's).
- `tag_key` (String) Narrow this condition to only the samples carrying this exact tag key=value pair (see `tag_value`). Must be given together with `tag_value`, or omitted along with it — the server rejects one without the other. Only meaningful for a `custom:<name>` metric_type; has no effect on a builtin metric or an SLO burn rate condition.
- `tag_value` (String) The tag value to match, paired with `tag_key` — see that attribute's own description.
- `window_minutes` (Number)
